title: Frontend's Consignment addresses page offers every unanswered party a link reading just "Add"; Design release 1 names the party in the link — "Add a place of origin", "Add a consignor"

finding.frontend: Every unanswered row on the Consignment addresses page carries one link and it reads "Add". The party is appended only as visually hidden text, so a sighted trader scanning the page meets six identical links reading "Add", one under each of Place of origin, Consignor or exporter, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination and County Parish Holding number (CPH). The string is one shared word for every row (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:6-7), applied at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/controller.js:41 with the row title pushed into visuallyHiddenText at :42.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 gives each row its own link text naming what is being added: "Add a place of origin", "Add a consignor", "Add a consignee", "Add an importer", "Add a place of destination" and "Add a CPH number". Each is a designed string held against the section it belongs to (app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:6, :19, :33, :46, :60, :74) and rendered as the row's only link (app/views/roles-and-addresses.html:104-106). Nothing is hidden: what a screen reader announces and what a sighted trader reads are the same words.
finding.difference: Give each unanswered row a link that names its party, using Design release 1's six strings, instead of the shared word "Add" with the party hidden. This is one new string per party in the addresses copy — the party table already holds a title per party at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/parties.js:20-57, so the link text can sit beside it — plus the CPH row's own string, and the Welsh counterparts. The visuallyHiddenText on the action then becomes redundant and should be dropped rather than doubled up. This is deliberately only about the unanswered rows: what an answered row shows is a separate and larger change, raised as addresses--hub-shows-only-the-party-name.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding any frontend addresses row whose visible link text names its party. The captured DOM of fe-addresses-hub renders six anchors whose visible text is exactly "Add", each followed by a govuk-visually-hidden span holding the lower-cased party name, and fe-addresses-hub-empty renders five of the same.
finding.verification: This finding arrived with its verification and correction slots already filled, so I checked it from scratch rather than reading them. Ran the falsifier: tag-stripping capture/html/frontend/fe-addresses-hub.html gives six rows each reading "Add" followed by a govuk-visually-hidden span holding the lower-cased party name — "place of origin", "consignor or exporter", "consignee", "importer", "place of destination", "county parish holding number (cph)" — and fe-addresses-hub-empty.html holds five of the same, with no CPH row because that commodity does not need one. Traced the frontend string to source: copy.add is the single word "Add" at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:7, applied at controller.js:41 with title.toLowerCase() pushed into visuallyHiddenText at :42. Read the six requirements-side strings at app/data/consignment-address-sections.js:6, :19, :33, :46, :60 and :74 and confirmed each renders as the row's only link in capture/html/prototype/dr1-roles-and-addresses.html. Opened evidence/prototype@491b3926/page/dr1-roles-and-addresses.png and read "Add a place of origin", "Add a consignor", "Add a consignee", "Add an importer", "Add a place of destination" and "Add a CPH number" as a sighted user meets them. Confirmed the citation is a root view, not a release subfolder. CORRECT.
finding.correction: It is deliberately scoped to the link text alone, and that scoping survives checking: it is a different change from addresses--hub-shows-only-the-party-name, which is about what an answered row shows, so the two are not one increment. Frontend's "Not added yet" value has no counterpart on the requirements side, but that follows from Frontend rendering this page as a govuk summary list where Design release 1 uses headed sections, and the component choice is not what this comparison is about — the link wording is separable from it, which is why it is here and the status word is not. One thing to know when reading the two cards side by side: the party name is present on the Frontend side too, in the anchor's visually hidden span, so a screen-reader user already hears "Add place of origin". What changes is whether a sighted user reading down the page can tell six identical links apart. One further copy difference on this page, checked and folded in here rather than given a row of its own because it is a single character: Frontend's fraud warning ends with a full stop — "Providing a false address is an act of fraud." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/copy/copy.en.js:4) — and Design release 1's does not (app/views/roles-and-addresses.html, rendered in dr1-roles-and-addresses). Whoever edits this copy file for the link text should drop it at the same time. Apart from that and the CPH row's capitalisation, which addresses--cph-wording owns, every heading and hint on the two pages matches word for word.

relatedTo.why: Both change how one row of the Consignment addresses page reads, one in its answered state and one in its unanswered state, and they should be written as one piece of copy work.
